action: Pharmacies: uninstall old remote-access tools when a provider changes tools, require human validation of remote sessions, and keep several backup copies.
date_note: Publication date of the Pharma365 interview; the intrusion date is not stated (owner was alerted on a Sunday)
exec: A pharmacy's backups were copied through a forgotten remote-access tool, a risk for any small health business.
plain: A pharmacy in Dijon says an intruder logged in and copied its backups. Dispensing and billing carried on, and the owner says patients were not affected.

key_findings: Owner Jean-Olivier Mariani says an intruder logged in while the pharmacy was closed and copied backups; there was no outage.
He was alerted by a colleague who saw the pharmacy listed on a LinkedIn page about cyberattacks.
He attributes it to an old remote-access tool not being removed after a provider switched tools; IT vendor Pharmaland traced it within hours.
Complaint filed with police; the ARS was informed.
recommendations: Non-native remote-access tools uninstalled; remote connections need human validation; more backup copies.

summary: Pharma365 interviews the owner of Pharmacie des Congrès in Dijon, who says an intruder logged into the pharmacy's system while it was closed and copied its backups. He says dispensing and billing were unaffected and blames a remote-access tool left installed after a provider changed tools. A police complaint was filed.
title: Dijon pharmacy says intruder logged in and copied its backups

validation.note: Single trade-press interview with the owner; no authority statement read.
